s1.syndrome_frame: Acute kidney injury with hemolysis in a patient on rifampin therapy
salient_findings: Acute kidney injury with elevated creatinine
Hemolysis with low haptoglobin and elevated lactate dehydrogenase
key_facts: 29-year-old woman from the Dominican Republic
Moved to the United States in 2014
Presented in January 2016 for prenatal care
Purified protein derivative skin test was positive (21 mm)
Started on rifampin (300 mg daily) for a planned 4-month course in January 2022
Experienced nausea, vomiting, and subjective fevers after three months of therapy
Initial presentation showed no significant physical examination findings
Baseline creatinine was 0.96 mg/dL in January 2022
Creatinine increased to 3.8 mg/dL at Emergency Department presentation in April 2022
Blood urea nitrogen was 41 mg/dL at Emergency Department presentation
Platelets were 84 K/μL at Emergency Department presentation
Aspartate aminotransferase was 115 U/L at Emergency Department presentation
Hemoglobin was 12.1 g/dL at Emergency Department presentation
Haptoglobin was <10 mg/dL at Emergency Department presentation
Lactate dehydrogenase was 1125 U/L at Emergency Department presentation
Urine protein was 102.7 mg/dL at Emergency Department presentation
Mild hematuria was present at Emergency Department presentation
Renal ultrasound showed markedly echogenic renal cortices bilaterally, consistent with parenchymal disease

shortlist.label: Rifampin-induced hemolytic anemia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient experienced hemolysis while on rifampin therapy

shortlist.label: Rifampin-induced acute interstitial nephritis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient developed acute kidney injury while on rifampin therapy

shortlist.label: Hemolytic uremic syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with hemolysis, thrombocytopenia, and acute kidney injury

shortlist.label: Autoimmune hemolytic anemia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had a positive purified protein derivative skin test and developed hemolysis

shortlist.label: Acute tubular necrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had a significant increase in creatinine and urine protein, consistent with acute kidney injury

raw.rationale: The patient's laboratory results, including low haptoglobin, elevated lactate dehydrogenase, and hemoglobinuria, are consistent with hemolytic anemia, which is a known side effect of rifampin. The renal biopsy findings of tubules containing eosinophilic proteinaceous material and cell debris, with strong reactivity for hemoglobin by immunohistochemistry, further support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Rifampin-induced acute interstitial nephritis
rejected.why: While the patient's renal function declined, the biopsy findings do not support acute interstitial nephritis, and the presence of hemolytic anemia is more consistent with rifampin-induced hemolytic anemia.

rejected.label: Hemolytic uremic syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's laboratory results do not show the typical schistocytes seen in hemolytic uremic syndrome, and the renal biopsy findings are not consistent with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Autoimmune hemolytic anemia
rejected.why: The patient's hemolytic anemia is more likely related to rifampin use, given the temporal association and the presence of other laboratory findings consistent with rifampin-induced hemolytic anemia.

rejected.label: Acute tubular necrosis
rejected.why: The patient's renal biopsy findings do not support acute tubular necrosis, and the presence of hemolytic anemia is more consistent with rifampin-induced hemolytic anemia.
